steps.description: Choose appropriate tool: pandas for data analysis, openpyxl for formulas
Thoroughly inspect the Data sheet to understand row layout, series codes, and year columns

suggestions: Before writing any formulas, print a sample of the Data sheet: identify the exact row numbers for each series code and the column letters for each year.
Verify which rows correspond to Exports (BXGS), Imports (BMGS), and GDP (NGDPD) for each country.
warnings: The single most common failure is incorrect INDEX/MATCH ranges — wrong row ranges produce values off by orders of magnitude (e.g., 25 instead of 404). Verify all ranges before writing formulas.

steps.description: Load the existing workbook for modification
Write INDEX/MATCH lookup formulas for all three data blocks, then statistics and weighted mean

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ CRITICAL: Never hardcode computed values. Use Excel formulas like '=INDEX(Data!$H$21:$M$40, MATCH(D12, Data!$B$21:$B$40, 0), MATCH(H9, Data!$H$4:$M$4, 0))' so the lookup is dynamic.

suggestions: Use INDEX/MATCH with exact row/column ranges: INDEX(Data!$H$<start>:$M$<end>, MATCH(series_code_cell, Data!$B$<start>:$B$<end>, 0), MATCH(year_cell, Data!$H$4:$M$4, 0)).
Double-check the Data row ranges for each block (Exports rows 21–26, Imports rows 28–33, GDP rows 35–40) — wrong ranges produce values off by 10x–100x.
warnings: Verify ranges match actual Data sheet structure by checking sample values before writing all 30 formulas.

steps.description: Verify recalc output and spot-check lookup values against known expected values

failure_patterns.reason: ❌ Read the recalc.py JSON output — check 'status' and 'total_errors'. If errors_found, fix and re-run.

suggestions: Spot-check: H12 (UAE Exports 2019) should be ~404. If you see ~25, the MATCH lookup is hitting the wrong rows — fix the range.
Confirm recalc shows 'status: success' and 'total_errors: 0' before finishing.
